descrizione: wild spiky jet-black hair bursting out in big pointed tufts above a deep petrol-teal bandana tied around the forehead with two long tails flying behind his head, big bright dark eyes under thick angled eyebrows, a huge open toothy grin, a small beige plaster across the bridge of his nose, big head about 45 % of height on a short cartoon body, light tan sun-kissed skin, a sleeveless burnt-orange canvas vest worn open on his bare chest, a worn cream canvas satchel with a petrol-teal patch and a wooden toggle hanging on his left hip from a rope-beige strap across his chest from the right shoulder, rolled-up knee-length petrol-teal trousers held up by a thick knotted rope belt with hanging ends, cream cloth wraps around both wrists, barefoot
carattere: A cheeky, cheerful harbour street-kid of about 17 who grew up on the docks of a Ligurian fishing village: reckless, generous, always grinning, climbs and swims like a monkey.
nota: STORICO IDEE, NON È IL PROTAGONISTA UFFICIALE (è lo scugnizzo del molo, personaggio di prova di Alberto). Il protagonista ufficiale è `personaggi/protagonista-pixellab/`. Personaggio di Alberto (birbasan) col suo Claude, nato il 02/11/2026. Lo spirito è quello di Rufy di One Piece senza copiarlo (un copricapo che lo fa riconoscere, pochi colori forti, vestiti aperti, sorrisone), con un po' di Goku bambino (capelli a punte, ingenuo e forte). Direzione scelta: lo scugnizzo del molo (bandana con le code al vento, scalzo, cima da ormeggio come cintura), arancio e petrolio. Gradino 0: tre varianti A/B/C con F3 come metro, scelta la A (02/11); poi la A con l'accessorio, scelta la A2 con la borsa a tracolla (design/scugnizzo_design.jpg). Il bastone resta un'idea per l'arma in mano (armi a strati). Modello in 5 viste e camminata a 8 pose in 9 viste (108 sprite, 48 px, 20 colori, 16 direzioni) fatti il 02/11/2026; provato nel Borgo col banco, ok di Alberto (02/11/2026); da far vedere a Jack e Riccardo. Nome segnaposto.

mosse.cammina: WALK CYCLE, 4 frames: right foot forward contact, passing pose with the legs together, left foot forward contact, passing pose with the legs together, arms swinging opposite to the legs (frame 2 is also the standing pose)
mosse.passo1: PROFESSIONAL WALK CYCLE, FIRST STEP, 4 frames that continue into the next row, a relaxed natural walk with a clear up-and-down bounce: 1) CONTACT: the RIGHT leg reaches forward straight with only the HEEL touching the ground and the toes lifted, the other leg straight behind pushing on its toes, the legs at their widest, the arm opposite to the front leg swung forward and the other arm swung back; 2) DOWN, the LOWEST pose: the front foot now flat on the ground taking the weight with that knee bent, the whole body and the head about 2 pixels LOWER than in frame 1, the back foot peeling off the ground, the arms at their widest swing; 3) PASSING: the supporting leg straight under the body, the other leg bent at the knee with its foot lifted and passing beside the supporting ankle, the arms passing close to the body; 4) UP, the HIGHEST pose: rising on the toes of the supporting leg, now a little behind, the body and the head about 2 pixels HIGHER than in frame 1, the free leg swinging forward and reaching out for the next step, the arms swinging the other way. ARMS, very important: a BIG clearly readable arm swing opposite to the legs, both arms always visible OUTSIDE the torso silhouette and never hidden behind the body, the forward hand well in front of the body and the back hand well behind it at the widest poses (in front and back views the two hands show at the two sides of the body, one swung forward and up, the other swung back), the arms passing beside the hips in the passing pose, the arm positions changing smoothly from frame to frame
mosse.passo2: PROFESSIONAL WALK CYCLE, SECOND STEP: the same 4 poses as the row above with the legs and the arms swapped, 4 frames, after frame 4 the cycle loops back to frame 1 of the row above, a relaxed natural walk with a clear up-and-down bounce: 1) CONTACT: now the LEFT leg reaches forward straight with only the HEEL touching the ground and the toes lifted, the other leg straight behind pushing on its toes, the legs at their widest, the arm opposite to the front leg swung forward and the other arm swung back; 2) DOWN, the LOWEST pose: the front foot now flat on the ground taking the weight with that knee bent, the whole body and the head about 2 pixels LOWER than in frame 1, the back foot peeling off the ground, the arms at their widest swing; 3) PASSING: the supporting leg straight under the body, the other leg bent at the knee with its foot lifted and passing beside the supporting ankle, the arms passing close to the body; 4) UP, the HIGHEST pose: rising on the toes of the supporting leg, now a little behind, the body and the head about 2 pixels HIGHER than in frame 1, the free leg swinging forward and reaching out for the next step, the arms swinging the other way. ARMS, very important: a BIG clearly readable arm swing opposite to the legs, both arms always visible OUTSIDE the torso silhouette and never hidden behind the body, the forward hand well in front of the body and the back hand well behind it at the widest poses (in front and back views the two hands show at the two sides of the body, one swung forward and up, the other swung back), the arms passing beside the hips in the passing pose, the arm positions changing smoothly from frame to frame IMPORTANT: this second step is NOT a mirror image of the row above. The whole body, the head and the face keep EXACTLY the same orientation toward the camera as in the row above (the same side of the head, the same cheek and the same ear stay visible in every frame of every row, the character never turns his head or shoulders to the other side); only which leg and which arm is forward changes.
mosse.missile: MAGIC MISSILE CAST, a quick one-handed cast that sends a bolt of magic flying STRAIGHT ahead of him, 4 frames drawn with the classic animation principles: 1) ANTICIPATION, the aiming pose that is held longest: the weight on the back foot, the knees a little bent, the body leaning back and slightly turned, compact and coiled (squash), the RIGHT arm pulled back with the elbow bent and the open hand with spread fingers beside his right shoulder, the LEFT arm stretched forward pointing at the target for balance, the head level and the eyes on the target in front of him; 2) CAST: a quick forward lunge, the front foot stepping forward, the RIGHT arm thrust STRAIGHT out in front of him at shoulder height with the palm open and facing forward and the fingers spread, the whole body stretched long and leaning into it (stretch), the LEFT arm swung back, the bandana tails still flying back behind the head (overlapping action); 3) FOLLOW-THROUGH: the right arm still held out with the wrist flicked up and the fingers wide open, the body at its longest reach over the bent front knee, the bandana tails and the open vest swinging forward past the body; 4) RECOVER: the right arm coming down toward the hip, the body straightening up and the weight coming back to the middle in a relaxed ready stance, both arms near the body. The right arm moves on a round arc, the left and right arms are never mirror images of each other, the head keeps the same size in every frame. The burnt-orange open vest, the petrol-teal bandana with its two tails, the cream satchel on its rope strap, the rolled-up petrol-teal trousers, the rope belt and the bare feet with cream cloth wraps keep exactly the same colours as in the walk; ABSOLUTELY NO effects of any kind: no glow, no energy ball, no sparks, no light rays, no flames, no lightning, no smoke, no swoosh or arcs, no motion blur, no speed lines, no impact splash, no dust, no particles; the hands are bare and EMPTY (nothing in them, the spell itself is added later by the game); nothing in any frame is cyan, glowing or magical-coloured, the only colours are the character's own
mosse.bomba: MAGIC BOMB LOB, a big slow OVERHEAD throw of a heavy invisible magic bomb up in a high arc, 4 frames drawn with the classic animation principles: 1) ANTICIPATION, a big wind-up: crouching with the knees well bent, the body leaning back and twisted away from the target (squash: low and coiled), the RIGHT arm swung far back and low behind his hip with the hand curled as if gripping a heavy ball, the LEFT arm stretched forward pointing at the target; 2) THROW: unwinding and rising, the front foot stepping forward, the RIGHT arm whipping up and forward over his shoulder and stretched HIGH up in front of him with the hand opening at the release, the body stretched tall and long (stretch), the LEFT arm pulled back for balance; 3) FOLLOW-THROUGH: the right arm swinging down across his chest toward his left hip, the body bent forward over the bent front knee, the back foot lifting off the ground behind him, the bandana tails and the open vest swinging forward past the body (overlapping action); 4) RECOVER: straightening up with both feet on the ground, the arms relaxed in front of the body, the weight in the middle in a ready stance. The throwing arm moves on a big round arc over his head, the left and right arms are never mirror images of each other, the head keeps the same size in every frame.
